items.question: Kalshi K8: start at $8 a bet (not $15) and step up with the cash: $10 from $67, $15 from $100?
items.why: $15 a bet on $55 means 3 losses in a row (the test had a streak of 8) leave too little to bet. Betting about 15% of the cash keeps the pot alive while it grows.
items.impact: Chance the $55 is wiped out in the first 4 weeks: 7.9% -> 0.2% as tested, 24.8% -> 3.3% if the edge is half as good; median after 4 weeks $467 -> $430 (-$37) if the edge holds.
items.applies: the K8 page's own bet pick ($5 / $8 / $10 / $15): pick $8 Monday, move up by the ladder (no code change); an automatic ladder in engine/kalshi_clock.py only after your yes
items.risk: If the edge is real you grow a bit slower in week 1-2 (about $37 less after 4 weeks); if it fades you lose $10-20 instead of the whole $55
items.recommend_why: Same money within 8% when it works, about 25-40x less chance of being wiped out before it can work. The pot is too small for $15 bets.
items.valued: 2026-11-20 tools/money/kalshi_bankroll.py (the 105 held-out + 128 earlier K8 bets of the 3 live legs, whole days resampled, 20,000 paths of 20 trading days, fees and real prices in)
items.closed_note: Replaced the same night by the K8 bot's own sizing (night-kalshi8, engine/kalshi_clock.py BANKROLL): each bet = 4.5% of the cash ($2.50 at $55, grows by itself as the cash grows), with stops at 15% a day, 25% a week and 35% from the peak. An $8 bet would trip the day stop after one loss, so the bot itself would refuse a second $8 bet.
